Subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation follow-up

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Call recap:
- You confirmed FinSecure needs strict tenant data isolation for production PII workloads and would prefer network-level separation where possible.
- Current constraints: security team requires customer-managed KMS for at-rest encryption and audit logs retained for 7 years.
- You asked whether Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) is sufficient or if Private VPC/on-prem is required for compliance.

Short answers:
- Dedicated: provides physical reservation of GPU capacity and logical separation, but still runs in Redwood-managed VPCs. Good for isolation and predictable performance; can be paired with strict tenancy and encryption options.
- Private VPC/on-prem: gives you a customer-controlled network boundary (VPC peering or on-prem deployment), optional customer-managed KMS/HSM, and tighter control over egress. Recommended if your compliance team requires the control-plane and network to be entirely within customer-managed networks.

Requested next steps:
1) I'll share a short matrix that maps your requirements (KMS, audit retention, network egress, logs access) to Dedicated vs Private options.
2) Propose a technical follow-up with our SE (Vivek) to walk through architecture and the deployment checklist.
3) If it helps, I can send our SOC 2 summary and a Private deployment checklist for your security review.

Can we schedule the SE call for next week? I included Tom to help coordinate with your infra team.

Thanks,

Thanks — great questions. Short answers below and proposed agenda for the SE call.

Answers:
- Dedicated network isolation: Dedicated capacity gives you dedicated GPU pools and per-customer tenancy at the runtime layer. Network is still in Redwood-managed VPCs, but we can implement strict subnet allocation and security groups to prevent tenant-to-tenant traffic; there's no shared tenant networking at the IP layer. That said, if your auditors require the VPC to be in your control or to be peered into your own account, Private VPC is the option.
- KMS/HSM: Private VPC supports customer-managed KMS integrations (bring-your-own KMS) and HSM for key custody. For Dedicated we offer customer key wrapping/Bring Your Own Key in partnership with cloud KMS, but not an HSM appliance in the same way as Private on-prem. We'll document exact key flow for the call.
- Audit logs: We can provide detailed request-level audit logs and configurable retention. For Dedicated we support retention up to N years (we'll confirm limits), and for Private deployments you can retain logs in your own storage for arbitrary retention periods.

Proposed SE call agenda (45 min):
1) Architecture overview (Dedicated vs Private) — 10 min (Vivek)
2) KMS/HSM keyflow and options — 10 min (Vivek)
3) Audit logs, retention, and log delivery options — 10 min (Marissa/Vivek)
4) Compliance checklist and next steps — 10 min

I've attached the SOC 2 summary and our private deployment checklist for your review. If that looks ok, Vivek can present the architecture on the call.

When are you available Wed/Thu next week? I can propose 10:00 or 14:00 PST.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Sarah / team — Vivek (SE) here. Adding a few technical clarifications ahead of the call and attaching a short architecture diagram.

Technical highlights to help your security review:
- Network isolation: Dedicated capacity provides physical separation at the compute level (dedicated GPU host pools) and logical tenant isolation in the runtime. Networking is managed by Redwood, but we offer per-customer subnet allocation and strict Security Group/ACL controls; traffic can be restricted to specific egress ranges.
- Private VPC: we support two patterns — customer VPC peering (Redwood deploys control/ingress in our control plane but data plane sits inside your VPC) or fully on-prem appliance for air-gapped needs. Both options allow you to keep control-plane access restricted to your network and to manage routing policies.
- KMS/HSM: For Dedicated we support BYOK via cloud KMS key-wrapping; keys are usable from Redwood-managed instances but keys remain in your KMS. For Private deployments we can integrate with customer HSMs or an HSM-backed KMS for FIPS/HSM-backed key custody.
- Audit & logs: We can stream raw audit logs (request IDs, timestamps, full event metadata) to your S3/GCS/Azure blob or to a SIEM via secure forwarders. Retention is configurable; for Dedicated we typically provide up to 7 years via managed archive, but for Private you control retention fully.
- Egress and data residency: Private VPC makes egress control explicit; we can restrict all egress to your networks and provide egress-only NAT in your account.
